title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 14-16). On p. 14 Grothendieck starts from a set 𝓕 of 'figures' with two order relations: ≤ (thought of as inclusion) and ≪, where F ≤ G ⇒ F ≪ G, so ≪ is coarser than ≤. From these he defines a subset 𝓜 ⊂ 𝓕 of 'points' (eq. 1.20) and a further subset 𝓛 ⊂ 𝓜 (eq. 1.25). He then embeds 𝓕 into P(𝓜) by F ↦ F̃ = {X ∈ 𝓜 | X ≤ F}, and into 'figures of 𝓜' by Fig_𝓜(F) = {X̃ | X ∈ F̃}. Under the first embedding ≤ becomes inclusion: F ≤ G ⇔ F̃ ⊂ G̃.

This page.
(1) Self-critique of the second relation. In contrast with ≤, the relation ≪ has no simple direct interpretation. It cannot be read off from the subsets F̃ ⊂ M, nor from the 'multi-déploiements' (or similar word) Fig(F). In particular G ≪ F does not imply Fig_M(G) ≪ Fig_M(F), so ≪ is not transported by the second embedding. He concludes that using ≪ there, and the identification notation = Fig_M(F), are 'perhaps a bit bogus' ('bidon').
(2) Reformulation with the points M as primary data (1.33). The structure becomes:
- a family 𝓕 ⊂ P(M) of subsets of M;
- an order relation ≪ on 𝓕 implied by inclusion (written F ≤ G).
He finds this less attractive, both for simplicity of data and because ≪ has no evident set-theoretic meaning at first sight. He then says this is where 'the (big) openings' ('ouvertures') will serve, apparently to motivate introducing ≪ (marginal note).
(3) First axiom on (1.33), completed on p. 16. 𝓕 should be a family of '(pré)admissible' subsets of M that induces a preorder on M, namely the specialization preorder y ≤ x iff every F containing x contains y. This preorder must actually be an order. Concretely:
- (i) for each x, 𝓕^x = {F ∋ x} has a least element F_x, which equals M_{≤x};
- (ii) x ↦ F_x is injective, i.e. a T0 separation condition.
The margin warning 'attention au "pr"' flags the préordre/ordre (or préadmissible/admissible) distinction.

Overall this is a change of primitive data: from an abstract pair of orders on 'figures' to a poset M of points with a distinguished family of closed (down-)sets plus an extra relation. It belongs to Grothendieck's 1986 attempt at a combinatorial/'tame' axiomatics of Analysis situs (figures, points, closures). The duality used is the classical one between T0 Alexandrov-type families of closed sets and posets.
errors: No mathematical error. The page is an explicit self-correction: he notes that G ≪ F does not imply Fig_M(G) ≪ Fig_M(F), so the earlier notation is misleading.
The meaning of ≪ is never specified on this page; the reformulation (1.33) leaves ≪ as unconstrained extra data, a gap he acknowledges.

ideas.what: Recovering an order on points from a family of subsets: least member F_x of {F ∋ x}, with injectivity of x ↦ F_x (T0) making the specialization preorder an order
ideas.modern_name: Specialization preorder / Alexandrov (finite T0) space–poset correspondence
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. Alexandrov (1937); McCord, Stong (1966) for finite spaces
ideas.where_published: Specialization order appears in EGA I (0_I 2.1) for schemes; this axiomatic use is only in unpublished notes

ideas.what: Representing abstract 'figures' as subsets of a set of points via F ↦ F̃ = {X ∈ M | X ≤ F}, turning ≤ into inclusion
ideas.modern_name: Representation of a poset by down-sets of its join-irreducible/point elements (Birkhoff-type representation)

ideas.what: A second, coarser order ≪ on figures implied by inclusion, recognised as having no direct set-theoretic interpretation
ideas.modern_name: Closest perhaps: adherence/frontier relations in stratified or tame spaces; unclear
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 is related in spirit only

missed.claim: An axiomatic 'analysis situs' in which figures carry, besides inclusion, a second order ≪ not determined by the underlying point sets. Grothendieck notes this extra relation is not functorial for Fig_M and leaves its meaning to be justified by 'ouvertures'. It is part of the unpublished 1986 tame-topology foundations, which nobody has developed.
missed.quote: ainsi G ≪ F n'implique nullement Fig_M(G) ≪ Fig_M(F). Aussi l'utilisation ≪ et la notation = Fig_M(F) sont-ils peut-être un peu bidon!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is of minor interest for combinatorial or o-minimal foundations of stratified spaces, but too sketchy here to constitute a result.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a notational self-critique and a restatement of standard poset/T0 closed-set duality. The only unpublished element is the undefined auxiliary relation ≪, which carries no content on this page.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'Par contre la relation ≪ n'a [pas] d'interprétation ... simple directe' rather than 'pour écrire la relation ≪ ni [?]'.
'en termes des F ⊂ M' presumably refers to the subsets F̃ ⊂ M.
'prédmissibles' is probably 'préadmissibles' (cf. margin 'attention au "pr"!' and p. 16 'n'est jamais admissible').
'multi-diplogement' / 'diplogéométrique' are uncertain readings; possibly forms of 'déploiement'. Illegible, so treat as unknown.
